where students can buy and sell items on campus, or describe what it really does. ## Final Year Project My final year project is SentinalGuard, which is still going on. SentinelGuard is an AI-assisted Zero Trust framework that checks every control command before it reaches a physical actuator, such as the pump in a smart irrigation system. It follows a PIP → PDP → PEP pipeline. The PIP, a FastAPI and MQTT backend, collects the sensor readings and packages them as evidence. A cross-sensor Reliability Layer, trained on normal data only, and an AI Risk Model (Random Forest or XGBoost) then score each command. The PDP decides whether to allow, restrict or block it, and the PEP on the ESP32 enforces that decision. It targets sensor spoofing, sensor replay, command replay and stealthy spoofing (test cases C0 to C4). So far we have prepared SWaT Stage 1 data (FIT101, LIT101, P101, MV101) as a time-ordered normal/early-attack/late-attack split to validate the method. The next step is to recalibrate and retrain on our own hardware readings, because SWaT’s values and dynamics differ from our small sensors. ## My favorite subjects My favorite subjects are Information security and Cyber forensics becuase in these we studied how to make the information secure and how to do forensics after any cyber attack.

# RAG for Student Career Anxiety (Cloud Computing Project) ## What it is For my Cloud Computing course, I created a RAG system for the topic of student career anxiety. RAG stands for retrieval-augmented generation. Instead of letting a language model answer only from its own memory, a RAG system first searches a collection of documents for the passages that match the question and then gives those passages to the language model so that it can answer based on them. ## Why I chose student career anxiety Many students worry about their future jobs, skills and results. I wanted to build a helper that gives calm, relevant guidance on that topic. ## How it works 1. Documents about career anxiety are collected and split into smaller chunks of text. 2. Each chunk is stored so it can be searched, for example with keyword search or with embeddings that capture meaning. 3. When a student asks a question, the system retrieves the most relevant chunks. 4. A language model reads those chunks and writes an answer based on them. ## Tools and cloud services the language model: Gemini AI, embedding model, vector store, cloud platform and programming language you used: python ## What I learned about RAG Building this showed me that the quality of a RAG answer depends a lot on the documents and on how they are chunked. # SentinalGuard (Final Year Project, In Progress) ## What it is SentinalGuard is my final year project (FYP) at the University of Management and Technology. It is still going on, so it is not finished yet. SentinelGuard is a security layer for a smart irrigation system. It checks every command, such as “turn the pump on”, before it reaches the hardware, and blocks it if it looks fake or unsafe. It uses AI together with a Zero Trust rule: never trust a command until it has been verified. ## The problem Smart irrigation systems send sensor readings and commands over the network, so an attacker can spoof a sensor, replay old readings, or replay old commands. A fake command can make the pump run at the wrong time, which wastes water or damages crops. Many existing systems only detect attacks, and few stop them before they reach the hardware. ## What it does The system is a pipeline. An ESP32 sends sensor readings over MQTT to a FastAPI backend (the PIP), which collects them. Two AI parts then score each command, and a decision layer (the PDP) allows or blocks it. The ESP32 (the PEP) enforces that decision. I worked on the AI part, so the data, features and model steps below are the ones I did or planned. ## My role and my team I am handeling the AI/ML brancg of the project. currently i am working on the dataset.

# Smart Environment Control System (Digital Logic Design Project) ## What it is The smart environment control system was my project for Digital Logic Design (DLD). It detects the temperature of the environment and turns LED lights on according to the temperature ranges I defined. It can also detect the humidity in the environment. The system uses sensors, LEDs and a buzzer. ## How it works A temperature sensor measures how hot or cold the surroundings are, and a humidity sensor measures how much moisture is in the air. The system compares the readings with ranges that I set in advance. Depending on which range the temperature falls into, a different LED lights up, so a person can understand the condition of the room at a glance. The buzzer is used as an alert. When the temperature or humidity goes above a limit, the buzzer on. ## Components I used - Sensors for temperature and humidity - LEDs for the different temperature ranges - A buzzer for alerts - a microcontroller, logic gates, resistors, breadboard ## Why this project fits digital logic design DLD is about how inputs are turned into outputs through logic. In this project the sensor readings are the inputs, and the LEDs and the buzzer are the outputs. Deciding which output turns on for which input range is a decision-making circuit, which is exactly what logic design teaches.
